key_insight: AHOY reconstructs complete, animatable 3D human avatars from in-the-wild monocular videos with heavy occlusion by combining a Gaussian-splat representation with video diffusion priors to plausibly fill unobserved regions and enable animation.
problem_solved: Existing 3D human reconstruction methods require largely unoccluded, canonical-pose footage; AHOY addresses the challenge of building full, animatable avatars when large body regions are never observed in monocular, in-the-wild videos (e.g., YouTube clips).
method: Represent the subject as a 3D Gaussian-splat avatar optimized from monocular video frames for fast, view-consistent rendering.
Use video diffusion priors to hallucinate and regularize plausibly missing geometry and appearance in heavily occluded regions across frames.
Enforce temporal and pose consistency and rigging (animatable topology) so the reconstructed avatar can be driven/animated post-reconstruction.
impact: Enables building realistic, animatable human avatars from abundant real-world footage (e.g., YouTube) despite occlusions, lowering data requirements and expanding applicability to downstream AR/VR, games, and content creation workflows.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input occluded video -> Gaussian-splat reconstruction -> video-diffusion inpainting -> animatable avatar
Before/after examples: frames showing heavy occlusion vs completed 3D avatar render from novel views
Animation overlay: skeleton/pose-driven animation of the reconstructed avatar to show animatability
Comparative chart: qualitative/quantitative comparison with baseline methods on occluded footage
paper_title: AHOY! Animatable Humans under Occlusion from YouTube Videos with Gaussian Splatting and Video Diffusion Priors
paper_authors: Aymen Mir, Riza Alp Guler, Xiangjun Tang, Peter Wonka, Gerard Pons-Moll
